output.summary: KEP-1179 proposed adding a pseudo build tag (build constraints) to in-tree cloud provider code so Kubernetes can be built without in-tree cloud providers, to simulate their future removal. The KEP's status is implemented, stage stable.
output.rationale: The in-tree cloud provider code is being removed (KEP-2395), and hidden uses via side channels such as init() methods are hard to find without a build that excludes it. A build tag lets the team verify removal and gives smaller binaries for cloud-provider-less clusters, with no change to default builds. The status reasons come from the review thread on PR #3007, which concerned how status values map to KEP stages rather than this KEP's technical merits.

alternatives.option: Wait for the in-tree providers to be removed entirely
alternatives.why_not: The readme says this 'may not provide sufficient tools to adequately prepare', and the providers are not guaranteed to exit at the same time.

alternatives.option: Each cloud provider duplicates the work to test a cloud-provider-free Kubernetes
alternatives.why_not: The readme names this as a risk, since each provider would need its own duplicate effort.

alternatives.option: Maintain a branch or PR carrying the removal changes
alternatives.why_not: The readme says that would be expensive to maintain and would obscure the effort, so developers would have little visibility that their changes were cloud-provider related.

evidence.quote: We will add a build constraints to the cloud provider code for a pseudo "build tag" specifying not to include any in-tree provider code.
in the default mode without our pseudo-tag the code will build as today and require zero additional maintenance to function.
https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/2598 is the PR that moved this KEP to implemented. It landed after
